Bill.BriefDescription: Changing duties for aiding injured persons.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to failing to summon assistance; adding newsections to chapter 9A.36 RCW; and prescribing penalties.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 9A.36 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: A person is guilty of the crime of failing to summon assistance if: (1)(a) He or she was present when a crime was committed againstanother person; or (b) he or she was made aware that a crime wascommitted against another person by someone who was present when thecrime was committed against the other person; and (2) He or she knows that the other person has suffered substantialbodily harm as a result of the crime committed against the other personand that the other person is in need of assistance; and (3) He or she could reasonably summon assistance for the person inneed without danger to himself or herself and without interference withan important duty owed to a third party; and (4) He or she fails to summon assistance for the person in need;and p. 1 SHB 1236 (5) Another person is not summoning or has not summoned assistancefor the person in need of such assistance.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 9A.36 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: A violation of section 1 of this act is a misdemeanor.
